title: BotDojo Launch: Enhancing AI Assistants with Evaluations and Synthetic Data
talk_summary: A live demo of BotDojo, a low-code LLM app builder, showing how to run batches of test questions through a chatbot flow, score them with evaluations (hallucination, retrieval sufficiency), then generate synthetic test data from real support tickets to improve the flow. The core mechanism is turning production traffic into a regression eval set and closing the loop by generating missing knowledge documents.

takeaways.technique: Batch eval runs over a question set with per-node traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Runs a whole batch of questions through the flow and scores each with evaluations, with per-node traces showing exactly what was sent to the LLM and what the retriever returned.

takeaways.technique: Mine real support tickets into Q&A test data
takeaways.what_they_do: Extracts questions and answers from live support-ticket conversations and uses them as realistic test inputs to the chatbot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you extract questions and answers from support tickets. So, these are live agents talking with customers and you use this as a test data

takeaways.technique: Synthetic data generation to fill retrieval gaps
takeaways.what_they_do: A generation flow takes the failing questions, pulls relevant context from the existing index, writes a document in the same style, and inline-evaluates whether the document actually answers the question before indexing it.

takeaways.technique: Compare batch runs before/after a change
takeaways.what_they_do: Clones a batch, changes one variable (data filter, model, throughput), reruns, and compares old vs new results side by side.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm going to compare um the the batch that we ran before with the new stuff.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every node's exact LLM input, retriever output, and raw data is inspectable as a trace, used for debugging apps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can pull a trace of each node and see exactly what we sent to the LLM, what came from the retriever, the exact, you know, data, which has been super useful for debugging apps
